draft.title: The anaerobic glycolysis system
card: The anaerobic glycolysis system remakes ATP by breaking down glucose without using oxygen. Anaerobic means without oxygen.
It supplies most of the energy for hard efforts lasting about 10 seconds to two minutes, such as a 400 metre run.
It makes ATP faster than the aerobic system, but it makes only a small amount from each unit of glucose.
It produces by-products, including lactate and hydrogen ions. These build up in the muscles and are linked to fatigue, which forces the athlete to slow down.
draft.remember: Glucose without oxygen: fast ATP for hard efforts, but by-products build up and cause fatigue.

a.q: Which description fits the anaerobic glycolysis system?
opts: It breaks down glucose without oxygen for hard efforts
It breaks down glucose with oxygen for steady efforts
It uses stored fuel in the muscle for a few seconds
It breaks down fats without oxygen for long efforts
a.why: The system uses glucose and does not need oxygen, so it suits hard efforts of about 10 seconds to two minutes. The option about oxygen and steady efforts describes a different kind of system, because anaerobic means without oxygen.

b.q: Kai runs a hard 400 metre race in about 55 seconds. His legs feel heavy and he slows in the last 50 metres. Which explanation fits the anaerobic glycolysis system?
opts: By-products built up in his muscles as the system made ATP
His body ran out of glucose to make ATP in the final stretch
The system stopped working once oxygen reached his muscles
The system made ATP too slowly to support a hard effort
b.why: A 55 second hard effort relies mostly on this system, which produces by-products such as lactate and hydrogen ions. These build up in the muscles and are linked to fatigue. The system makes ATP quickly, so slow ATP supply is not the reason, and the card does not say glucose runs out.
b.clue: Think about what the system produces as well as ATP.

a.best: It breaks down glucose without oxygen for hard efforts

b.best: By-products built up in his muscles as the system made ATP

problems.detail: The card says the by-products are 'linked to fatigue, which forces the athlete to slow down'. 'Forces' overstates the link. Current science does not treat lactate as a direct cause of fatigue. Use 'can make the athlete slow down'.

The remember line says the by-products 'cause fatigue', but the card says only that they are 'linked to fatigue'. The remember line states a stronger causal claim than the card supports. Use 'are linked to fatigue'.

check.summary: Both questions are sound. The card's 'forces the athlete to slow down' and the remember line's 'cause fatigue' overstate a link the card otherwise describes only as 'linked to fatigue'.

Remember, other: The remember line says the by-products 'cause fatigue', but the card says only that they are 'linked to fatigue'. The remember line states a stronger causal claim than the card supports. Use 'are linked to fatigue'.
